correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the concept class as inclusion-maximal independent sets, not maximum independent sets or neighborhoods. Independently tested each trace T on an independent support S of size at most five by branching on witnesses: every omitted vertex must have a neighbor in an independent set containing T and avoiding S minus T. This condition is necessary and sufficient by maximal extension, so the test does not depend on enumerating the supplied concept list. It recovers the four face vectors (1,2), (1,4), (1,8,16), (1,16,88,160,104); no size-five face shatters and larger ones are excluded by heredity. The facet size-counts are respectively {1:2}, {1:4}, {2:16}, {2:8,4:104}. The union of the four stated isometry orbits equals the actual Q4 facets, with sizes 8,16,24,64, and the distance test agrees for every triple. All cube automorphisms are translations followed by coordinate permutations: an automorphism fixing zero is determined by its permutation of the neighbors, since the distance vector to zero and its neighbors determines any vertex. This proves the first nonpure case with the scope stated, not a pattern for larger cubes. The Python 3.8 minimum in the notes is too low for int.bit_count(), but the complete finite certificates are otherwise appropriately described. value.rationale: The useful result is a complete symmetry-reduced criterion for every query support, together with the first failure of purity along a natural sequence, not another measurement of the number of maximal independent sets or the already shared Q4 coefficient vector. In dimension four an antipodal pair becomes a genuine smaller maximal face even though larger faces exist; this identifies exactly how equal-size facets, and hence matroidal structure, fail at the boundary. Choosing one representative per isometry orbit makes the classification usable in subsequent comparisons with perturbations.
